gate1.baseline_note: Current working tree baseline includes the accepted shared slow-trend allocation stack through exp-20260515-018.

gate_questions.1_alpha_hypothesis: risk allocation: signals that are both RS60 top-quintile leaders and top-quartile price-vs-200MA extension leaders may deserve a tiny extra allocation.
gate_questions.2_history_check: The component states were accepted separately, close-location/range/volume/candidate-pool branches were rejected or data-limited, and no direct overlap risk scout was found.
gate_questions.4_acceptance_standard: docs/backtesting.md three fixed windows; aggregate EV/PnL positive, at least two EV-improved windows, no EV-regressed windows, survival >= 5%, max drawdown drift <= 0.5 pp, nonzero adjustments.

historical_experiment_check.why_this_branch: It follows the playbook's allocation-before-filtering prior and tests an orthogonal production-visible overlap rather than another scalar retune, LLM branch, or noisy universe expansion.

hypothesis: The current accepted stack rewards RS60 leadership and price-vs-200MA extension independently. The remaining alpha question is whether their intersection identifies a smaller set of persistent slow-trend leaders that can support a tiny additional cap-aware sizing top-up without adding filters or expanding the candidate pool.
interpretation: Dual slow-trend leadership did not clear the canonical three-window gate; do not add an extra overlap top-up on the frozen windows.
